changes.reason: Use analytic s, p and d projectors on Na (9 functions) so the d-hybridised conduction states get their own functions instead of making the 3p functions more diffuse.
Keep the frozen edge that gave the best eta_2 so far (E_F+4.5 eV). It contains the Fermi level, and validate_deck shows it holds at most 3 states against 9 functions.

diagnosis: eta_2 is too high because the 4-function sp model does not interpolate well between mesh points. The subspace and the spread minimisation are not the cause. Both minimisations converged monotonically. On the 11×11×11 construction mesh, every state below the frozen edge is reproduced to about 1e-5 eV. The error appears only on the separate path: band 5, the band crossing E_F, is off by 40–60 meV within ±0.5 eV of E_F and by up to 190 meV near E_F+1.7 eV around H–N. This is the error you get when the hoppings decay too slowly for the mesh. The three p-like functions have spreads of 7.0 Å², and they carry all of the hopping weight beyond L_BvK/4. The fitted decay length is 2.7 Å, and cutting the hoppings at r_c raises eta_2 to 185 meV. Raising dis_froz_max from 2.08 to 4.5 eV improved eta_2 by only 2.7 meV, and the frontier's projectability ladder either refused to run or gave the same 41.4 meV. So the windows and thresholds are spent. What limits the result is the basis: the Na 3p functions are diffuse and are being forced to also describe the d-hybridised states above E_F. The pseudopotential has no d orbitals, so this cannot be fixed inside PDWF.

band_interpolation_eta2.note: eta_2 = 2.97 meV at mu = E_F(scf) + 2 = 3.555 eV over 270 path k-points and 9 bands
band_interpolation_eta2.insulator_rule: no band crosses E_F on the mesh and gap >= sigma = 0.1 eV
